'''Marcos Henrique "Didi" Louzada Silva''' (born 2 July 1999) is a Brazilian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Franca Basquetebol Clube|Sesi Franca]] of the [[Novo Basquete Brasil]] (NBB). At the [[2019 NBA draft]], he was drafted by the [[Atlanta Hawks]], before being traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].

== Early life ==
Louzada was born in [[Cachoeiro de Itapemirim]] in the Brazilian state of [[Espírito Santo]]. The first sport he played was [[futsal]], but he decided to focus on basketball when he was 10 years old.<ref name="interview">{{cite web|last1=Balassiano|first1=Fábio|title=Ala de Franca, Didi chama atenção aos 19 anos e projeta próximos passos da carreira|url=https://balanacesta.blogosfera.uol.com.br/2018/11/05/didi/|publisher=[[Universo Online]]|date=11 May 2018|access-date=10 May 2019|language=pt}}</ref> Louzada saw immediate success playing basketball for his school and joined the Liga Urbana Social de Basquete (LUSB) at age seven. He moved to NBB club [[Franca Basquetebol Clube|Franca]] in January 2015 and initially played for the under-16 team. After one season, he competed in the [[Liga de Desenvolvimento de Basquete]] (LDB), an under-22 league, and led his team to a championship.<ref name="pacheco">{{cite web|last1=Pacheco|first1=Felipe|title=Capixaba de 17 anos vira promessa do basquete|url=https://tribunaonline.com.br/capixaba-de-17-anos-vira-promessa-do-basquete|publisher=Tribuna Online|date=10 October 2016|access-date=10 May 2019|language=pt|archive-date=10 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510202235/https://tribunaonline.com.br/capixaba-de-17-anos-vira-promessa-do-basquete|url-status=dead}}</ref> In August 2016, Louzada was one of 40 players invited to the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) Americas Team Camp in [[Mexico City]].<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA to bring fourth edition of Americas Team Camp presented by Nike to MexicoCity|url=https://pr.nba.com/americas-team-camp-mexico-city/|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|date=3 August 2016|access-date=10 May 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Franca (2017–2019)===
Louzada made his NBB debut for Franca on 16 February 2017, playing under two minutes in a 99–78 win over [[Esporte Clube Pinheiros (basketball)|Pinheiros]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Feb 16, 2017 - Pinheiros/Sky 78 at France 99|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-02-16/Pinheiros-Sky-at-Franca/255566|publisher=[[RealGM]]|date=16 February 2017|access-date=10 May 2019}}</ref> On 26 January 2019, he recorded a career-high 27 points and six rebounds in a 100–70 victory over Nicaraguan club [[Real Estelí F.C.|Real Estelí]] in the [[FIBA Americas League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Invicto, Sesi Franca garante classificação na Liga das Américas|url=http://www.cbb.com.br/noticias/2019/01/invicto-sesi-franca-garante-classificacao-na-liga-das-americas|publisher=[[Campeonato Brasileiro de Basquete]]|date=28 January 2019|access-date=10 May 2019|language=pt|archive-date=10 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510202235/http://www.cbb.com.br/noticias/2019/01/invicto-sesi-franca-garante-classificacao-na-liga-das-americas|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Jan 26, 2019 - France 100 at Real Esteli 70|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-01-26/Franca-at-Real-Esteli/329324|publisher=[[RealGM]]|date=26 January 2019|access-date=10 May 2019}}</ref>

On 12 April 2019, Louzada played for the World Select Team at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]] in [[Portland, Oregon]].<ref name="suaide">{{cite web|last1=Suaide|first1=Pedro|title=NBA: Didi, de Franca, é chamado para treino pré-draft, revela choro ao ver seu nome em rankings e abre seus sonhos|url=http://www.espn.com.br/nba/artigo/_/id/5425830/nba-didi-de-franca-e-chamado-para-treino-pre-draft-revela-choro-ao-ver-seu-nome-em-rankings-e-abre-seus-sonhos|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=25 March 2019|access-date=10 May 2019|language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=12 April 2019 |title=2019 Nike Hoop Summit: World Select Team Announced |url=http://www.nikehoopsummit.com/images/2019%20NIKE%20HOOP%20SUMMIT%203_22.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210609041601/https://www.nikehoopsummit.com/images/2019%20NIKE%20HOOP%20SUMMIT%203_22.pdf |archive-date=2021-06-09 |access-date=10 May 2019 |publisher=[[Nike Hoop Summit]]}}</ref> On 19 April, he declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]]. At the time, Silva was ranked by [[ESPN]] as the 61st-best prospect in the draft class.<ref name="draft">{{cite web|last1=Givony|first1=Jonathan|title=Brazilian Silva declares eligibility for NBA draft|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26545862/brazilian-silva-declares-eligibility-nba-draft|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=17 April 2019|access-date=10 May 2019}}</ref> Silva was selected as the 35th pick of the 2019 NBA draft by the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. His draft rights were later traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-rights-alexander-walker-hayes-silva|title=Pelicans acquire rights to Alexander-Walker, Hayes, Silva|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2019|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref>

===Sydney Kings (2019–2021)===
On 5 July 2019, Louzada signed with the [[Sydney Kings]] in the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL), a league based in Australia. Silva joined the team through the NBL Next Stars program, which was created in the previous year to attract NBA draft prospects to the NBL.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcos 'Didi' Louzada Silva joins Sydney Kings as part of NBL's Next Stars program|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/marcos-didi-louzada-silva-joins-sydney-kings-as-part-of-nbls-next-stars-program/news-story/7ab7e8a9d26a55198dabb2dbb9f7561a|work=FOX Sports|date=July 5, 2019|access-date=July 5, 2019}}</ref> He averaged 10.6 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.6 assist per game. On 30 September 2020, Louzada re-signed with the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Didi Louzada Returning to Sydney|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/didi-louzada-returning-to-sydney|website=NBL.com.au|date=30 September 2020|access-date=17 December 2020}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2021–2022)===
On 27 April 2021, Louzada signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Didi Louzada|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-didi-louzada|website=NBA.com|date=27 April 2021|access-date=27 April 2021}}</ref> On 19 November, he was suspended for 25 games for violating the terms of the NBA's anti-drug program.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NBA suspends Pelicans' DiDi Louzada for 25 games|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-suspends-pelicans-didi-louzada-for-25-games|url-status=live|access-date=November 19, 2021|website=NBA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119221311/https://www.nba.com/news/nba-suspends-pelicans-didi-louzada-for-25-games |archive-date=2021-11-19 }}</ref> On 21 January 2022, while playing in the [[NBA G League]] for the [[Birmingham Squadron]], Louzada suffered a left knee injury. Two days later, the Pelicans announced that he was diagnosed with a torn [[medial meniscus]] in his left knee and would be ruled out indefinitely.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Didi Louzada injury update |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/didi-louzada-injury-update |access-date=March 23, 2022 |website=New Orleans Pelicans}}</ref> On 4 February, he underwent surgery on his left knee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pelicans' Didi Louzada: Undergoes successful surgery |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pelicans-didi-louzada-undergoes-successful-surgery/ |access-date=March 23, 2022 |website=CBS Sports|date=4 February 2022 }}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2022)===
On 8 February 2022, the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] acquired Louzada, [[Nickeil Alexander-Walker]], [[Tomáš Satoranský]], [[Josh Hart]], a protected 2022 first-round draft pick, the better of New Orleans' and Portland's 2026 second-round draft picks and New Orleans' 2027 second-round draft pick from the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[CJ McCollum]], [[Larry Nance Jr.]] and [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]].<ref>{{Cite press release|date=February 8, 2022|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-complete-trade-new-orleans|title=TRAIL BLAZERS COMPLETE TRADE WITH NEW ORLEANS|publisher=Portland Trail Blazers}}</ref>

On August 29, 2022, Louzada was waived by the Blazers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Trail Blazers Waive Didi Louzada |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-didi-louzada |access-date=2022-09-25 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Cleveland Charge (2022–2023)===
On October 24, 2022, Louzada joined the [[Cleveland Charge]] training camp roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charge 2022 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-2022-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}}</ref>

===Flamengo (2023–2024)===
On June 29, 2023, Louzada signed with [[Flamengo Basketball|Flamengo]] of the [[Novo Basquete Brasil]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Flamengo acerta a contratação de Didi Louzada para a disputa da NBB|url=https://www.agazeta.com.br/mais-esportes/flamengo-acerta-a-contratacao-de-didi-louzada-para-a-disputa-da-nbb-0623|website=AGazeta.com.br|date=June 29, 2023|access-date=August 9, 2023|language=Portuguese}}</ref>

On June 13, 2024, Louzada was drafted by the [[Valley Suns]] in the [[2024 NBA G League expansion draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-25 NBA G League Expansion Draft|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2024-expansion-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 13, 2024|access-date=June 14, 2024}}</ref>

==National team career==
===Junior national team===
In 2014, Louzada joined the Brazilian national under-15 team at the FIBA South America Under-15 Championship in [[Barquisimeto]], Venezuela. In five games, he averaged 4.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game, while winning the gold medal over [[Argentina]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcos Silva's profile - 2014 South American U15 Championship for Men|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/118123/sid/10941/tid/250/_/2014_South_American_U15_Championship_for_Men/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105050049/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/118123/sid/10941/tid/250/_/2014_South_American_U15_Championship_for_Men/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 November 2015|publisher=[[FIBA]]|access-date=10 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2014 South American U15 Championship for Men|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/event/p/sid/10941/_/2014_South_American_U15_Championship_for_Men/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170220054715/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/event/p/sid/10941/_/2014_South_American_U15_Championship_for_Men/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 February 2017|publisher=[[FIBA]]|access-date=10 May 2019}}</ref> Louzada played for the [[Brazil national under-17 basketball team|Brazilian national under-16 team]] at the [[2015 FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]] in [[Bahía Blanca]], Argentina. In five games, he averaged 6.6 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 0.6 assists per game, as Brazil finished in sixth place.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcos Silva's profile - 2015 FIBA Americas U16 Championship for Men|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/118123/sid/8076/tid/250/_/2015_FIBA_Americas_U16_Championship_for_Men_FIBA_Americas_U16_Championship_for_Men/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510202235/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/118123/sid/8076/tid/250/_/2015_FIBA_Americas_U16_Championship_for_Men_FIBA_Americas_U16_Championship_for_Men/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 May 2019|publisher=[[FIBA]]|access-date=10 May 2019}}</ref><ref name="realgm">{{cite web|title=Didi Louzada Silva Player Profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Didi-Louzada-Silva/Summary/92177|publisher=[[RealGM]]|access-date=10 May 2019}}</ref>

===Senior national team===
On 10 September 2018, Louzada was called up to play for the senior [[Brazil national basketball team|Brazilian national team]] in the second phase of [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Americas)|2019 FIBA World Cup qualification]].<ref name="terra">{{cite web|title=Surpreso com convocação, Didi celebra chance de jogar ao lado de ídolos|url=https://www.terra.com.br/esportes/basquete/surpreso-com-convocacao-didi-celebra-chance-de-jogar-ao-lado-de-idolos,273ce1a35dc40314441c21a2efb392c4whs5ccmn.html|publisher=[[Terra (company)|Terra]]|date=10 September 2018|access-date=10 May 2019}}</ref> He made his debut three days later, playing less than a minute in an 85–77 loss to [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canada]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sep 13, 2018 - Brazil 77 at Canada 85|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2018-09-13/Brazil-at-Canada/288631|publisher=[[RealGM]]|date=13 September 2018|access-date=10 May 2019}}</ref> On 21 February 2019, he scored 15 points in a 104–80 win over the [[Virgin Islands national basketball team|Virgin Islands]], helping Brazil qualify for the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=McCarthy |first1=John |date=22 February 2019 |title=Virgin Islands Men's Basketball Team Dominated By Brazil 104-80 |url=http://vifreepress.com/2019/02/virgin-islands-mens-basketball-team-dominated-by-brazil-104-80/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510202234/https://vifreepress.com/2019/02/virgin-islands-mens-basketball-team-dominated-by-brazil-104-80/ |archive-date=2019-05-10 |access-date=10 May 2019 |website=Virgin Islands Free Press}}</ref>
